questions.question:
A solid conducting sphere, having a charge \(Q\), is surrounded by an uncharged conducting hollow spherical shell. Let the potential difference between the surface of the solid sphere and that of the outer surface of the hollow shell be \(V\). If the shell is now given a charge of \(-4Q\), the new potential difference between the same two surfaces is:
1. \(-2V\)
2. \(2V\)
3. \(V\)
4. \(4V\)
questions.explanation:
Hint:Shell will produce constant potential. Thus new potential difference = \(V\) Step: Find the new potential difference between the same two surfaces. Let a solid sphere of radius \(R_1\)have a charge\(Q\)and it is surrounded by an uncharged conducting hollow spherical shell of radius \(R_2\). The potential difference between a sphere and a spherical shell is given by; \(\Delta V = kQ_{in}\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1}-\dfrac{1}{R_2}\right)\) The inner surface of the hollow shell will still have a charge of \(-Q\), induced by the charge \(Q\) on the solid sphere. The outer surface of the hollow shell will now have a charge of \(-4Q+Q = -3Q\). The potential difference remains proportional to the original charge (i.e., charge on the conducting sphere) because the geometry and charges balance symmetrically. Therefore, the new potential difference between the same two surfaces is\(V.\) Hence, option (3) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
A solid sphere of radius \(R\) carries a charge (\(Q+q\)) distributed uniformly over its volume. A very small point like piece of it of mass \(m\) gets detached from the bottom of the sphere and falls down vertically under gravity. This piece carries charge \(q\). If it acquires a speed \(v\) when it has fallen through a vertical height \(y\) (see figure), then : (assume the remaining portion to be spherical).


1. \( v^2=2 y\left[\dfrac{q Q}{4 \pi \epsilon_0 {R}({R}+{y}) {m}}+g\right] \)
2. \( v^2=y\left[\dfrac{q Q}{4 \pi \epsilon_0 {R}^2 {ym}}+g\right] \)
3. \( v^2=2 y\left[\dfrac{q Q R}{4 \pi \epsilon_0({R}+{y})^3 {~m}}+g\right] \)

Hint: Apply the law of conservation of energy. Step:Find the speed acquired by the sphere. The electric potential energy of the falling charge \(q\) due to the remaining sphere of charge \(Q\) is given by; \(U_e = \dfrac{qQ}{4\pi \varepsilon_0 r}\) The initially electric potential energy is given by; \(U_{e~ i} = \dfrac{qQ}{4\pi \varepsilon_0 R}\) After falling a distance\(y\), the final electric potential energy is given by; \(U_{e~f} = \dfrac{qQ}{4\pi \varepsilon_0 (R+y)}\) Using conservation of energy we get; \(mgy + (U_{e~i}- U_{e~f}) = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2\) \(\Rightarrow mgy + \left(\dfrac{qQ}{4\pi \varepsilon_0 R}- \dfrac{qQ}{4\pi \varepsilon_0 (R+y)}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2\) \(\Rightarrow mgy + \left(\dfrac{qQy}{4\pi \varepsilon_0 (R)(R+y)}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2\) \(\Rightarrow v^2= 2y\left[g + \left(\dfrac{qQ}{4\pi \varepsilon_0 R(R+y)m}\right) \right]\) Hence, option (1) is the correct answer.
